mainTopic: Which injuries free a slave (castration and the tongue), and whether the tongue counts as exposed for טומאה, טבילה and הזאה
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא listing injuries that free a slave: cutting off an extra finger, which רב הונא limits to a finger that lines up with the others. Then the גמרא tells a story. The elders of נזוניא asked רב המנונא whether castrating a slave frees him, and he could not answer. רב חסדא answers it from a משנה listing the tips of limbs and a ברייתא built on it, where רבי adds castration. Since the organ is already on the list, רבי must mean the testicles. The גמרא then asks why רבי does not list the tongue, and concludes that he counts it all the more so. עולא teaches that everyone treats the tongue as exposed for טומאה and as hidden for טבילה. רבי and רבנן argue only about הזאה, based on how they divide a פסוק. Finally, a story about רבי's maidservant shows that hidden places need not get wet, but they must be places water could reach. This matches רבי זירא's rule about mixing a מנחה.

steps.title: An extra finger that was cut off frees the slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list: if a slave had an extra finger and the master cut it off, the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the slave had an extra finger and the master cut it off, the slave goes free because of these injuries.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that lists injuries a master causes that set his slave free. The last item is cutting off an extra finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think an extra finger is not a real limb, so losing it should not matter. The ברייתא rules that cutting it off still counts as losing a limb, and the slave goes free.

phrases.english: An extra finger, and he cut it off —
the slave goes out to freedom through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא listing injuries that free a slave
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting off a slave's extra finger frees him.

steps.title: Only if the extra finger lines up with the others
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the rule to an extra finger that sits in line with the other fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This applies only when the extra finger is counted along the back of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a condition to the extra-finger rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every extra growth counts. Only a sixth finger that stands in the row with the other fingers is treated as a real limb, so only cutting that kind off frees the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Is counted (lines up with the others)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
And that is when it is counted along the back of the hand.
phrases.notes: He means the extra finger sits in the same row as the other fingers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the extra-finger case from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra finger counts only if it lines up with the other fingers.
steps.whatToRemember: An extra finger frees the slave only when it sits in line with the regular fingers.

steps.title: The elders of נזוניא skip רב חסדא's lecture
steps.stepSummary: The elders of נזוניא did not attend רב חסדא's lecture, so he sent רב המנונא to ostracize them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The elders of נזוניא did not come to רב חסדא's lecture. He said to רב המנונא: Go and ostracize them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that sets up a question about freeing a slave. רב חסדא sends his student to deal with elders who stayed away from his lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Skipping a great רבי's lecture was seen as disrespect toward Torah scholars. That is why רב חסדא wanted them pushed away from the community.

phrases.english: The elders of Nezonya
did not come to Rav Chisda's lecture.
He said to Rav Hamnuna:
Go, ostracize them.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבֵי דְנָזוֹנְיָא לָא אֲתוֹ לְפִירְקֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New story that will lead into a question about slaves' injuries
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא orders the absent elders to be ostracized.

steps.title: רב המנונא asks why they stayed away
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא goes to the elders and asks why they did not come to the lecture.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and said to them: Why didn't the rabbis come to the lecture?
steps.whatsHappening: Before carrying out the order, רב המנונא first asks the elders why they stayed away. This sets up their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He speaks to them respectfully and calls them 'רבנן'. He wants to hear their side before taking action.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbis (a respectful way to address them)

phrases.english: He went and said to them:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתוֹ רַבָּנַן לְפִירְקָא?
phrases.english: What is the reason the rabbis did not come to the lecture?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתוֹ רַבָּנַן לְפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב המנונא follows up on רב חסדא's order
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the elders skipped the lecture

steps.title: Their complaint, and רב המנונא's offer
steps.stepSummary: The elders say רב חסדא never answered a question they asked. רב המנונא offers to answer it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Why should we come? We asked him something and he did not answer us. He said to them: Have you asked me anything that I did not answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The elders explain that they felt they had nothing to gain, because their question went unanswered. רב המנונא confidently invites them to ask him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the test that comes next. רב המנונא's bold offer makes his failure in the next step more striking.

phrases.english: They said to him: Why should we come?
For we asked him a matter
and he did not resolve it for us.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי בְּעֵיתוּ מִינַּאי מִידֵּי
phrases.english: He said to them: Did you ask me anything
that I did not resolve for you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They stayed away because רב חסדא did not answer their question.

steps.title: Does castration free the slave?
steps.stepSummary: The elders ask: if a master castrates his slave, is that like a visible blemish that frees him, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked him: A slave whose master castrated him in the testicles, what is the law? Is it like a visible blemish, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The elders ask רב המנונא their real question: does castration count as a visible blemish that frees a slave?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a slave goes free for losing a visible limb. Castration damages a body part that is usually covered, so the question is whether it counts like an open, visible blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: A visible blemish (out in the open)

phrases.english: They asked him:
A slave whose master castrated him in the testicles, what is the law?
Is it like a visible blemish, or not?
phrases.notes: The question is whether damage to a covered body part counts like the visible injuries.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ: עֶבֶד שֶׁסֵּרְסוֹ רַבּוֹ בַּבֵּצִים, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The elders take up רב המנונא's offer and ask their question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether castration counts as a visible blemish that frees a slave
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the legal question the rest of the story is built to answer.

steps.title: רב המנונא cannot answer and is teased
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא did not know the answer, and the elders joked about his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not know. They asked him: What is your name? He said: המנונא. They said: Not המנונא (hot fish), but קרנונא (cold fish).
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא has no answer, and the elders tease him with a pun on his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המנונא sounds like 'חם נונא', a hot, tasty fish. They call him 'קר נונא', a cold fish, hinting that he fell flat. רב חסדא gives the answer in steps 8–12.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it (he did not know the answer)

phrases.english: It was not in his hand.
phrases.notes: Meaning he did not know the answer.

phrases.english: They said to him: What is your name?
He said to them: Hamnuna.
They said to him: Not Hamnuna,
but rather Karnuna.
phrases.notes: A pun: חם נונא is 'hot fish' and קר נונא is 'cold fish'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the question from step 6 left unanswered
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב המנונא cannot answer; רב חסדא resolves the question in steps 8–12.

steps.title: רב חסדא points to a known משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא reports to רב חסדא, who says the answer comes from a known teaching. He begins quoting the משנה about twenty-four tips of limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב חסדא. רב חסדא said: They asked you something answered by a known teaching. As we learned: The twenty-four tips of limbs in a person do not become impure because of healthy flesh...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא begins solving the elders' question by quoting a משנה about צרעת. The quote continues in the next step, so this step only sets up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists twenty-four tips of limbs. These parts are shaped so that a spot on them cannot be seen all at once, so the rule of מחיה does not apply to them. רב חסדא will use this list to judge the castration question.

keyTerms.meaning: A known teaching (here, one connected to a משנה)
A patch of healthy flesh inside a צרעת spot, which is normally a sign of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted משנה is about צרעת (נגעים), not about slaves. רב חסדא is borrowing its list of limbs to answer the slave question.

phrases.english: He came before Rav Chisda.
He said to him: They asked you a teaching.
phrases.notes: He means the answer is already found in a known teaching.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: נגעים 6:7

phrases.english: Twenty-four tips of limbs in a person
all of them do not become impure because of healthy flesh,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב חסדא begins answering the unresolved question from step 6
steps.raayaObject: Whether castration counts as a visible blemish that frees a slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נגעים about the twenty-four tips of limbs that are not affected by מחיה

steps.title: The list of the twenty-four tips of limbs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes quoting the משנה that lists the twenty-four ראשי אברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the tips: the tips of the fingers and toes, the tips of the ears, the tip of the nose, the tip of the male organ, and the tips of a woman's nipples. רבי יהודה says: a man's nipples count too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא is still quoting the משנה he started in the previous step. He lists exactly which body parts count as the 'tips of limbs.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fingers and toes give twenty. The rest of the list is the ears, the nose, the organ, and a woman's nipples. רבי יהודה adds a man's nipples to the list. This list is the base that the next ברייתא will use for freeing an עבד.

keyTerms.meaning: The tips or ends of the limbs

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵם: רָאשֵׁי אֶצְבָּעוֹת יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם,
phrases.english: And these are they: the tips of the fingers and toes,
and the tips of the ears, and the tip of the nose,
and the tip of the organ, and the tips of the nipples of a woman.
phrases.notes: גוייה usually means 'body,' but here it means the male organ.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: also those of a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵם: רָאשֵׁי אֶצְבָּעוֹת יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה begun in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The elders' question about castration of an עבד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing the twenty-four ראשי אברים

steps.title: A ברייתא applies the list to freeing a slave
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says an עבד goes free for injury to any of these tips; רבי adds סירוס and בן עזאי adds the tongue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא was taught on it: for all of these, a slave goes free. רבי says: castration too. בן עזאי says: the tongue too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא that takes the same list and says that if a master damages any of these parts, the עבד goes free. Two תנאים add more items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key source: רבי says סירוס also frees the עבד. That sounds like a direct answer to the elders' question. בן עזאי adds the tongue, which the גמרא will discuss later.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא was taught about it

phrases.english: And it was taught about it:
For all of them, a slave goes out to freedom.
Rabbi says: also castration.
Ben Azzai says: also the tongue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא connected to the משנה just quoted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי's addition of סירוס

steps.title: Which kind of castration did רבי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of סירוס רבי was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי says castration too. Castration of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי's line again and asks what exactly he meant by castration. This sets up the next step, which decides the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if רבי means the kind of castration the elders asked about. So the גמרא must first pin down what 'castration' means here.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said (quoting an earlier source)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר אַף הַסֵּירוּס.
phrases.english: The Master said: Rabbi says: also castration.
Castration of what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר אַף הַסֵּירוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes רבי's addition in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which body part's castration רבי refers to

steps.title: It must mean castration of the testicles
steps.stepSummary: Castration of the organ is already on the list, so רבי must mean the testicles, which answers the elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say castration of the organ, that is the same as the 'tip of the organ' already listed. So doesn't it have to mean castration of the testicles?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out one meaning and lands on the other. This proves that castrating the testicles frees an עבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the organ is already covered by 'the tip of the organ' in the list, so רבי would be adding nothing. Therefore he must mean the testicles. That is exactly the case the elders asked about, so רב חסדא's source answers them.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, castrating the testicles frees an עבד. This answers the elders' question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the story: the answer רב המנונא could not give comes straight from a known ברייתא.

phrases.english: If you say castration of the organ, that is the same as the organ.
phrases.notes: He means it is already on the list as 'the tip of the organ,' so רבי would be adding nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not castration of the testicles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 and completes the proof for step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The elders' question: does castration free an עבד?
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's addition of סירוס, which must mean the testicles

steps.title: Doesn't רבי count the mouth as visible elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי leaves out the tongue, since in the laws of הזאה he seems to treat the tongue as a visible place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says castration too. But does רבי not count the tongue? A contradiction: if someone was sprinkling and the water landed on the person's mouth, רבי says it counts as sprinkling, and the חכמים say it does not. Isn't that talking about his tongue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבי added castration but not the tongue, like בן עזאי did. It brings a ברייתא about sprinkling purifying water that seems to show רבי does treat the tongue as visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הזאה, the water has to land on a visible body part. רבי says water landing on the mouth works, which sounds like he holds the tongue is visible. If so, he should also say cutting the tongue frees an עבד, yet he did not list it.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set them against each other (a contradiction)

phrases.english: Rabbi says: also castration.
And according to Rabbi, not the tongue?
And they raised a contradiction:
Here is one who was sprinkling
and the sprinkling landed on his mouth,
phrases.notes: 'His mouth' means the mouth of the person being purified.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: he has sprinkled.
And the Sages say: he has not sprinkled.
Is it not on his tongue?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the castration proof to a new question about רבי's view of the tongue.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's not listing the tongue in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In הזאה רבי treats water on the mouth (tongue) as landing on a visible place, so he should count the tongue as a visible blemish for freeing an עבד.

steps.title: The water landed on the lips, not the tongue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the הזאה case was about the lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was on his lips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the contradiction by saying the water landed on the lips. So רבי never said the tongue is visible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lips are on the outside of the face, so water landing there is on a visible place. That tells us nothing about the tongue, so רבי can still hold that the tongue is hidden.

phrases.english: No, on his lips.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by reading the case differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the contradicting source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water landed on the tongue, so רבי holds the tongue is visible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water landed on the lips, which are clearly visible; no proof about the tongue.

steps.title: If it means the lips, that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that answer: water on the lips obviously counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: On his lips? That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. If the case is the lips, why would רבי even need to say it works?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lips are plainly visible, so it seems no one would think the sprinkling fails. A ברייתא should not bother teaching something so obvious.

phrases.english: On his lips, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case was about the lips
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lips are obviously visible, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: Lips are sometimes closed, so it needed saying
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that lips count as visible even though a person sometimes presses them closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that since sometimes he presses his lips shut, they are not visible; so it teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the lips case is not obvious. This saves the 'lips' answer for now, but the next step knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person sometimes seals his lips tightly, one could think they are a hidden place. רבי teaches that the lips still count as visible. On this reading the ברייתא is about the lips, so it would give no proof that רבי counts the tongue. The next step challenges this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage the גמרא reads רבי's הזאה ruling as being about the lips, which count as visible even though they are sometimes closed. The next step knocks this reading down, and step 18 concludes that רבי does count the tongue.

phrases.english: What would you have said?
sometimes he presses his lips shut,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a reasonable mistaken assumption the source comes to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lips are sometimes sealed, so they might count as hidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lips count as a visible place for הזאה.

steps.title: Two teachings show רבי treats the tongue as exposed
steps.stepSummary: Two ברייתות show that רבי treats the tongue as an exposed body part. This knocks down the answer that the הזאה case was only about the lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא clearly says 'on his tongue' (sprinkled water on the tongue counts). Another ברייתא says that if most of the tongue was cut off it is a blemish, and רבי says this means most of the speaking part of the tongue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two teachings that show רבי really does treat the tongue as an exposed, visible body part. If so, the question returns: why doesn't רבי list the tongue among the parts that set a slave free?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says the sprinkling works 'on his tongue', not just on the lips. So the answer from Step 14 fails. The second ברייתא shows that for רבי, cutting off the tongue is a blemish (מום), which fits treating the tongue as an exposed part.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (a challenge from a source)
And it is further taught (a second proof)
most of the speaking part (the front part of the tongue used for words)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'on his tongue'!
phrases.notes: This is a teaching about the הזאה case from Step 13 that clearly says the water landed on the tongue, not the lips.

phrases.english: And it is further taught:
and one whose tongue was mostly removed,
phrases.notes: This comes from a list of blemishes that disqualify a כהן or an animal for a קרבן.

phrases.english: רבי says: most of the speaking part of his tongue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the 'lips' answer of Steps 14-16 and brings the question of Step 13 back.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי's הזאה case was only about the lips
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Explicit ברייתות show רבי treats the tongue itself as exposed, both for הזאה and for blemishes. So his leaving the tongue off the slave list cannot be explained that way.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: רבי says castration, and the tongue is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. רבי adds castration, and of course the tongue too. בן עזאי adds the tongue but not castration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it like this. רבי says a slave also goes free for castration, and the tongue does not even need to be said. בן עזאי says he goes free for the tongue, but not for castration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we understand the ברייתא. רבי agrees about the tongue; he just did not bother to say it because it is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, it looked as if רבי left the tongue out on purpose. Now his silence means 'all the more so': if castration counts, the tongue surely does. The real argument is only about castration: רבי includes it and בן עזאי does not.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is not even necessary to say (all the more so)
a תנא who argues with רבי in this ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, רבי says: castration,
and the tongue does not even need to be said.
בן עזאי says: the tongue,
but castration, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: סֵירוּס, וְלָא מִיבַּעְיָא לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 rejects the lips answer, this gives a new answer to the original question of step 13 by reinterpreting the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא (the tongue is left out because it is obvious, not because it is excluded)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי left the tongue off his list because he does not count it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי counts the tongue all the more so. Only בן עזאי rejects castration.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next two questions about the word 'אף' and the order of the opinions.

steps.title: What does 'also' in בן עזאי's words refer to?
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי's word 'אף' (also) adds to the first opinion in the ברייתא, not to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'also'? It goes back to the first opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees a problem coming. The ברייתא has בן עזאי say 'also the tongue', which sounds like he is adding to רבי. So it explains that 'also' refers to the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בן עזאי rejects castration, he cannot be adding to רבי's list. So his 'also' adds the tongue to the basic list of the first תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: also (a word that adds to someone else's list)
on the first one (the first opinion in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: And what is 'also'?
phrases.notes: In the ברייתא, בן עזאי says 'also the tongue', which sounds like he is adding to רבי.

phrases.english: It refers to the first one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the new reading of Step 18 against a problem in the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying which opinion a word refers back to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אף' means בן עזאי adds to רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אף' means בן עזאי adds to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Then בן עזאי should have been listed first
steps.stepSummary: If בן עזאי adds to the first opinion and רבי adds even more, בן עזאי's opinion should come before רבי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, בן עזאי's opinion should have been placed first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The natural order goes from small to large. First תנא קמא, then בן עזאי adds the tongue, then רבי adds castration too. But the ברייתא puts רבי first.

phrases.english: If so,
let it place בן עזאי's opinion first!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נַקְדְּמַהּ דְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of Steps 18-19 by asking about the order of the opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the new reading, בן עזאי's opinion is the middle step. It should therefore come before רבי's broader opinion.

steps.title: The order stayed as it was first taught
steps.stepSummary: The תנא learned רבי's opinion first and fixed it in place. He heard בן עזאי later and added him at the end. A taught text is not rearranged.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא heard רבי's opinion and fixed it in the text. Later he heard בן עזאי's opinion and taught it after. And a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the odd order as a matter of history: it reflects which opinion the תנא heard first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal order would put בן עזאי first. But once a teaching was set and learned, it was not changed, so people would not get confused. So the order does not show who is adding to whom.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher who arranged the ברייתא
and he fixed it in place
a taught text is not moved from its place (its wording is not rearranged)

steps.whatToRemember: The order of opinions in a teaching can reflect when the תנא heard them, not their logical order, because 'משנה לא זזה ממקומה'.

phrases.english: The תנא heard רבי's opinion and fixed it,
and then heard בן עזאי's opinion and taught it,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; it just means 'it'.

phrases.english: and a משנה does not move from its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 about the order.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the order by how the teaching was handed down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order must follow the logic of who adds to whom.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order follows when the תנא learned each opinion, and the fixed text was not rearranged.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains surprising orders of opinions in many places across ש״ס.

steps.title: עולא: everyone agrees the tongue counts for touching a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that for טומאה, everyone agrees the tongue counts as exposed when it touches a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Everyone agrees that for טומאה, the tongue counts as exposed when it comes to touching a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from עולא about the tongue, this time about becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even people who do not treat the tongue as an outer part for other laws agree that it counts for touching. So if a tongue touches a שרץ, the person becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: a dead creeping creature that makes things טמא
exposed, counted as an outer part

phrases.english: עולא said:
All agree about the tongue regarding טומאה
that it is exposed with respect to a שרץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּלָשׁוֹן לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument about whether the tongue is exposed to a case where everyone agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tongue that touches a שרץ makes the person טמא; for this, everyone agrees the tongue counts as exposed.

steps.title: The reason: the תורה says 'whom he touches'
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'אשר יגע בו'. Touching is what counts, and a tongue can touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The תורה says 'whom he touches', and the tongue can also touch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source and the reason for עולא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאה from touching, the פסוק only asks whether contact happened, not whether the part is visible. Since a tongue can touch things, it counts.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the slave or הזאה cases. Here the question is not whether the tongue is an outer part, only whether it can touch, and everyone agrees it can.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
'Whom he touches', says the Merciful One,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:11

phrases.english: and this one too is able to touch.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בּוֹ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural basis for עולא's statement in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that the tongue counts for טומאה from a שרץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 15:11, 'אשר יגע בו': the law depends on touching, and a tongue can touch.

steps.title: For immersion, the tongue counts as hidden
steps.stepSummary: עולא continues: for טבילה, everyone agrees the tongue is treated as a hidden body part.
steps.simpleTranslation: With regard to immersion, the tongue is treated as hidden.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the second half of his rule. For טבילה, the tongue does not need to touch the water, because it counts as a hidden part of the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, the tongue counted as exposed for טומאה. Now the same tongue counts as hidden for טבילה. So the tongue's status depends on which law we are dealing with.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה to become pure
Hidden, a part of the body that is inside and not exposed
Is considered like, is compared to

steps.confusionAlert: The tongue is not 'exposed' or 'hidden' in every case. For טומאה it counts as exposed, and for טבילה it counts as hidden. Each law has its own rule.

phrases.english: With regard to immersion –
it is considered like something hidden.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the tongue, which is still the subject from עולא's last statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues עולא's statement. After the rule for טומאה, he now gives the rule for טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טבילה, the tongue counts as hidden, so the water does not need to reach it.

steps.title: The verse shows that immersion only needs the outside of the body
steps.stepSummary: The source is 'ורחץ בשרו במים'. Just as 'his flesh' is on the outside, only the outside parts of the body need the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The תורה says 'and he shall wash his flesh in water.' Just as his flesh is on the outside, so too everything that needs the water is on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the tongue does not need the water during טבילה, and it answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the water must touch 'his flesh,' meaning the skin on the outside of the body. From this we learn that טבילה only needs the outside parts of the body. The tongue is inside the mouth, so it does not need to be reached.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Just as... so too, a way of comparing two things

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And he shall wash his flesh in water"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:13

phrases.english: the Merciful One said,
just as his flesh is on the outside –
so too everything is on the outside.
phrases.notes: He means everything the water has to reach. Body parts on the inside, like the tongue, are left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא ״וְרָחַץ בְּשָׂרוֹ בְּמַיִם״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 24, the same way step 23 gave the source for step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the tongue counts as hidden for טבילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'ורחץ בשרו במים': the water must reach 'his flesh,' which is on the outside

steps.title: The argument is only about sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that רבי and רבנן argue only about הזאה. רבי compares sprinkling to טומאה, and רבנן compare it to טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagreed about sprinkling. רבי compares it to impurity, and רבנן compare it to immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both sides agree about טומאה and טבילה, עולא points to the one place where they really argue: הזאה, the sprinkling of the water of the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling sits between the two rules we already know. רבי says it follows טומאה, where the tongue counts as exposed, so sprinkling on the tongue works. רבנן say it follows טבילה, where the tongue counts as hidden, so sprinkling on the tongue does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the water of the פרה אדומה on someone who is impure
Compares, treats one law like another

steps.whatToRemember: טומאה: the tongue counts as exposed (everyone agrees). טבילה: the tongue counts as hidden (everyone agrees). הזאה: רבי follows טומאה, and רבנן follow טבילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the argument much smaller. רבי and רבנן do not argue about what a tongue is. They only argue about which law sprinkling should be compared to.

phrases.english: They only disagreed
with regard to sprinkling.
Rabbi compares it to impurity,
phrases.notes: For טומאה, the tongue counts as exposed (step 22). So for רבי, sprinkling on the tongue works.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis compare it to immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out the two rules everyone agrees on, עולא narrows the argument down to sprinkling alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument about the tongue is only about הזאה. רבי treats it like טומאה, and רבנן treat it like טבילה.

steps.title: רבי's reading of the sprinkling verse
steps.stepSummary: Both sides argue about one פסוק. רבי reads 'וחטאו' together with the first half, which talks about sprinkling on the impure person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them argue about this verse: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one, etc.' רבי holds that the verse should be read: 'And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall purify him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the argument comes from how to read one פסוק. It starts with how רבי divides it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי attaches the words 'and he shall purify him' to the sprinkling on 'the impure one.' This connects sprinkling to טומאה. So the sprinkling works on any body part that can become impure, and that includes the tongue.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: And both of them disagree about this verse:
"And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:19

phrases.english: Rabbi holds:
"And the pure one shall sprinkle on the impure one
on the third day and on the seventh day
and he shall purify him,"
phrases.notes: רבי ends the phrase here. That ties the purifying to the sprinkling on 'the impure one,' so sprinkling is like טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for רבי's side of the argument in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's view that הזאה is compared to טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading 'וחטאו' together with 'והזה הטהור על הטמא'

steps.title: רבנן's reading of the sprinkling verse
steps.stepSummary: רבנן read 'וחטאו' together with the second half of the פסוק, which talks about washing in water, so sprinkling is like טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן hold that the verse should be read: 'And he shall purify him on the seventh day, and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows how רבנן divide the same פסוק in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן attach 'and he shall purify him' to the washing in water that comes after it. This connects sprinkling to טבילה. So the sprinkling has to land on an outside body part, and the tongue does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall wash his clothes
And he shall bathe in water

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on which half of the פסוק the word 'וחטאו' belongs to. If it goes with the sprinkling on the impure person, sprinkling is like טומאה (רבי). If it goes with the washing in water, sprinkling is like טבילה (רבנן).

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
"And he shall purify him on the seventh day
and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water."
phrases.notes: Here 'and he shall purify him' is joined to bathing in water, so sprinkling follows the rules of טבילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of the reading: after רבי's way of dividing the פסוק, the גמרא gives רבנן's way.
steps.raayaObject: רבנן's view that הזאה is compared to טבילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading 'וחטאו' together with 'וכבס בגדיו ורחץ במים'

steps.title: Why don't רבנן compare sprinkling to impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבנן do not compare הזאה to טומאה, the way רבי does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן too, why not compare sprinkling to impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבנן. Why do they connect sprinkling to washing in water, and not to becoming impure the way רבי does?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about both the impure person and the washing in water. רבי linked הזאה to the טומאה part, so the גמרא asks why רבנן did not make the same link.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of the purifying water (of the פרה אדומה)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis as well,
let them compare it to impurity?
phrases.notes: "It" means the sprinkling, הזאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבנן from Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבנן that compares הזאה to טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק also mentions the impure person, so הזאה could just as easily be compared to טומאה.

steps.title: Learn purification from purification
steps.stepSummary: רבנן prefer to compare one way of becoming pure to another way of becoming pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One should learn purification from purification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבנן. Sprinkling and immersion are both ways to become טהור, so it makes more sense to compare them to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה is about becoming impure, while הזאה and טבילה are both steps that make a person pure. Comparing two things of the same kind is the better comparison.

phrases.english: He should learn purification from purification.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical preference for a comparison between similar things
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe הזאה should be compared to טומאה, since both are mentioned in the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: הזאה is a purification, so it is compared to טבילה, the other purification.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי compare sprinkling to immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: why does רבי not compare הזאה to טבילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, why not compare it to immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around and challenges רבי. The "purification from purification" reasoning seems to work for him as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two kinds of purification are the best comparison, רבי should agree that הזאה is like טבילה. The גמרא wants to know why he links it to טומאה instead.

phrases.english: And Rebbi, let him compare it to immersion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same kind of question from Step 29 against רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's comparison of הזאה to טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The "purification from purification" reasoning should lead רבי to compare הזאה to טבילה.

steps.title: "And he shall wash his clothes" breaks off the topic
steps.stepSummary: For רבי, the words "וכבס בגדיו" start a new section, so the washing in water is cut off from the sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he shall wash his clothes" interrupts the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי. The words "and he shall wash his clothes" divide the פסוק into two parts, so sprinkling belongs with the first part, about the impure person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is based on reading the פסוק, not on logic. In רבי's view, the washing of the clothes divides the פסוק. The washing in water then becomes a new topic and cannot be connected back to the sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall wash his clothes (במדבר 19:19)

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן compare הזאה to טבילה because both are ways of becoming pure. רבי compares it to טומאה because "וכבס בגדיו" cuts the פסוק into two parts.

phrases.english: "And he shall wash his clothes" interrupted the topic.
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:19. These words come between the sprinkling and the washing in water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of how the פסוק is divided
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי should compare הזאה to טבילה, since both are purifications.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, "וכבס בגדיו" divides the פסוק, so הזאה goes with the earlier topic of טומאה.

steps.title: The story of the bone in the maidservant's teeth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי treats the mouth as hidden for טבילה. He once required a maidservant to immerse again because a bone was found between her teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי really hold that for immersion the mouth counts as hidden? But there was a story: רבי's maidservant immersed, came up, and a bone was found between her teeth, and רבי made her immerse again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to attack עולא's claim that everyone, including רבי, treats the mouth as hidden for טבילה. If the mouth does not need water, why did the bone matter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said in Step 24 that for טבילה the tongue counts as hidden, so water does not have to reach it. Yet רבי ruled that a bone inside the mouth ruined the טבילה. That ruling makes it seem that the inside of the mouth does count.

phrases.english: And does Rebbi hold, regarding immersion,
that it is considered hidden?
phrases.notes: "It" is the tongue, from עולא's statement in Step 24.

phrases.english: But didn't Ravin say in the name of Rav Adda
who said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak:
There was an incident with a maidservant of Rebbi's household
who immersed, and came up,
and a bone was found between her teeth,
and Rebbi required her to immerse again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי לְעִנְיַן טְבִילָה כְּטָמוּן דָּמֵי? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to עולא's statement about טבילה (Step 24) and challenges it from a story about רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי agrees the mouth is treated as hidden for טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the inside of the mouth did not count for טבילה, a bone stuck in the teeth would not have required a new טבילה.

steps.title: Water need not reach it, but it must be able to reach it
steps.stepSummary: Water does not actually have to enter the mouth, but the mouth must be a place that water could enter. The bone blocked that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, we do not need the water to actually get in, but we do need the place to be fit for water to get in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Hidden places like the mouth do not need water to reach them, but nothing may block them so that water could not reach them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer makes a distinction. The water actually arriving is not required, but the place being open to water is required. The bone made that spot closed off, so the טבילה was not valid. This fits both עולא and the story.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא now says water must enter the mouth. It still does not have to. The mouth only has to be open, with nothing blocking it, so that water could get in.

phrases.english: Granted that we do not require the water to actually enter,

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם הָרָאוּי לָבוֹא בּוֹ מַיִם בָּעֵינַן,
phrases.english: we do require a place that is fit for water to enter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between actual contact and being fit for contact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the mouth is hidden, anything stuck inside it should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water does not need to reach hidden places, but they must be fit for water to reach. Something blocking them invalidates the טבילה.

steps.title: Support from רבי זירא's rule about mixing
steps.stepSummary: The idea that a place must be fit even if the water does not actually come is the same as רבי זירא's rule about mixing flour and oil in a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבי זירא, who said: whatever is fit to be mixed, the mixing does not hold it back; whatever is not fit to be mixed, the mixing does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a general rule from רבי זירא. The rule comes from the mixing of flour and oil in a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מנחה could have been mixed, it is still valid even if the mixing never happened. If it could not have been mixed at all, it is invalid. In the same way, a hidden place in the body does not need water, but it must be a place that water could reach.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing flour with oil in a מנחה
Holds back, makes it invalid if missing

steps.whatToRemember: Being able to do something can count even when it was not actually done. Mixing a מנחה does not have to happen, but it must be possible. Water does not have to reach the mouth, but it must be able to reach it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from רבי זירא is a tool used in many places: what matters is whether something is possible, even if it was not actually done.

phrases.english: As in the statement of Rabbi Zeira.
For Rabbi Zeira said:
Anything that is fit for mixing,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a מנחה, where flour is mixed with oil.

phrases.english: the mixing does not hold it back.
And whatever is not fit for mixing,
the mixing does hold it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 34 with a parallel general rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a hidden place must be fit for water even though water does not have to reach it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's rule about בילה in a מנחה: being fit matters even when the action was not done.
